picks.showTitle: Chinmaya Mission - Gita, Upanishads and Ancient Knowledge
picks.title: What Lies Beyond Worldly Pleasure?| Essence of the Geeta | Episode 86
picks.summary: Swami Swaroopananda, Global Head of Chinmaya Mission, is a revered spiritual leader known for his clear, profound Vedanta teachings. His wisdom guides many towards self-discovery and inner peace, making complex concepts accessible and inspiring globally. In this series, Swamiji distills the learnings from the Bhagavad Geeta and explains it in a way that allows everyone to enjoy the essence of the Geeta.
picks.reason: Swami Swaroopananda explains Bhagavad Gita's teachings on transcending worldly pleasure.

picks.title: Chapter 16, verses 1,2 and 3
picks.summary:
Bhagavad Gita Ch. 16 “Yoga of Divine and Devilish Estates” Verses 1, 2, & 3
The lecture discusses twenty-six qualities described as a person's divine estate, acquired through interaction with Prakriti and necessary for liberation from the limitations imposed by the ignorance of the Self.
Moksharthi - Please visit YouTube for Bhajans by Neil Bhatt - https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL8jOW56VdfinQGoaP3cRFi-lSBfxjflJE
Gita for Daily Living - Now on YouTube! https://www.youtube.com/@GitaforDailyLiving
picks.reason: Lecture on Bhagavad Gita's divine and devilish qualities relevant to liberation.

picks.title: Never Do An Enemy A Small Injury
picks.summary: “The thoughts of My pure devotees dwell in Me, their lives are surrendered to Me, and they derive great satisfaction and bliss enlightening one another and conversing about Me.” (Lord Krishna, Bhagavad-gita, 10.9)
picks.reason: Quotes Bhagavad Gita on devotees' surrender and bliss, touching on bhakti.

picks.title: Five Things You Seem To Have No Problem Finding Time For
picks.summary: “After attaining Me, the great souls, who are yogis in devotion, never return to this temporary world, which is full of miseries, because they have attained the highest perfection.” (Lord Krishna, Bhagavad-gita, 8.15)
picks.reason: Discusses Bhagavad Gita's view on liberation and perfection through devotion.

picks.title: 1818: Why Nothing in This World Satisfies Us
picks.summary: Voltaire — the greatest writer of the French Enlightenment wrote that there is a dim flame burning in every heart — an intuition that somewhere there is a home, a happiness that is real and lasting.  We spend our lives chasing it in bodies, children, homes, wealth, relationships. And it never quite delivers. In this episode Raghunath and Kaustubha explore that intuition, what covers that dim light, and how the sacred texts of the bhakti tradition say it can be uncovered. picks.reason: Discusses human dissatisfaction and bhakti teachings from Srimad Bhagavatam.
